execution_order:
  note: >
    Execution order prioritizes foundational sections first (theory
    in §3 establishes framework that §4-§6 reference). §7 Discussion
    and §1 Intro written after body is stable. Abstract last.
    Quality over speed — each step validated before proceeding.

  - step: 1
    task: "Rewrite method.tex with Information Bottleneck"
    task_type: paper_writing
    file: method.tex
    description: >
      HIGHEST PRIORITY — foundational section that §4-§6 depend on.
      (a) Remove CJT subsection, Mirage Hypothesis, Finding boxes.
      (b) Keep SICA pipeline (§3.1) with equations.
      (c) NEW §3.2 "The Information Bottleneck":
          - Causal DAG (TikZ, two-panel: self-extraction vs cross-arch)
          - SCB proof (Proposition: BR ≥ 1 under same-trace coupling)
          - CIL definition + CCR operationalization
      (d) §3.3 Experimental Setup (merge from experiments.tex §4.1).
      Worker must understand the proof logic thoroughly.
      Read paper-writing-norms.skill.md + paper-quality-lessons.skill.md.

  - step: 2
    task: "Rewrite experiments.tex → Results"
    task_type: paper_writing
    file: experiments.tex
    description: >
      (a) Remove §4.1 Setup (now in §3.3).
      (b) Keep Table 1 (tab:main_results).
      (c) Move regime-dependent analysis HERE from analysis.tex.
      (d) Move regime scatter figure HERE.
      (e) Condense TOST/power to 2-3 sentences.
      (f) Oracle: 1-2 sentences (details in appendix).
      (g) Reference §3.2 theory: "Proposition 1 predicts BR > 1;
          Table 1 confirms no positive effect."

  - step: 3
    task: "Rewrite analysis.tex → The Symbolic Mirage"
    task_type: paper_writing
    file: analysis.tex
    description: >
      (a) Rename section to "The Symbolic Mirage".
      (b) §5.1: Frame SCB as empirical VALIDATION of §3.2 theory.
          "Proposition 1 predicts BR ≥ 1; we observe 1.66-4.97x."
          Keep frontier-scb table, shuffle control, Z3 vacuity.
      (c) Process-kappa: condense to 3 sentences (move figure to appendix).
      (d) §5.3: EXPAND remediation (25-30 lines). Connect to CIL:
          "No training-free method achieves CIL > 0."
      (e) §5.4: Diagnostic framework with decision tree (TikZ inline).
          Connect to CIL: "diagnostics approximate CIL at zero cost."
      (f) Remove: Effective-K subsection (absorbed into §4).

  - step: 4
    task: "Rewrite solutions.tex with capability gap theory"
    task_type: paper_writing
    file: solutions.tex
    description: >
      (a) Open with capability gap derivation [Direction C]:
          ΔCombo ≈ V_acc - SC_G. State as "first-order approximation."
          Empirical validation: breakeven prediction matches data.
      (b) Soften claims: "preliminary evidence", "consistent with".
      (c) Add caveat: "significant only for Mistral-7B (SC below verifier)."
      (d) Fix data values if D152 patch not applied.
      (e) Connect to CIL: "CIL > 0 when V independent (Table in Appendix D)."

  - step: 5
    task: "Expand discussion.tex"
    task_type: paper_writing
    file: discussion.tex
    description: >
      From 2 to 4 paragraphs (~0.6 pages).
      (a) Diagnostics as practitioner tool (60/60, zero-cost).
      (b) Test-time scaling implications (K_eff ≤ 3.6 → redundancy).
      (c) Broader: SCB applies to any self-extracted structured repr.
      (d) Future: trained extractors, CIL as evaluation criterion.
      Remove \\enlargethispage hack.

  - step: 6
    task: "Rewrite introduction.tex"
    task_type: paper_writing
    file: introduction.tex
    description: >
      (a) Sharper hook: Z3 formal solver paradox.
      (b) CJT as 2 sentences (not a subsection reference).
      (c) Mention information bottleneck framework briefly.
      (d) Contributions: 3 items, max 3 lines each.
          C1: Symbolic Mirage (theory + empirics).
          C2: Diagnostic framework (60/60).
          C3: Cross-architecture escape (preliminary).
      (e) Add power caveat. Soften cross-architecture.
      (f) Keep Figure 1 (pipeline).

  - step: 7
    task: "Trim related_work.tex"
    task_type: paper_writing
    file: related_work.tex
    description: >
      (a) Merge CJT paragraph into SC paragraph.
      (b) Cut positioning by 50%.
      (c) 3 tight paragraphs total.
      (d) Reference our information bottleneck where positioning
          against Huang et al.

  - step: 8
    task: "Rewrite abstract.tex"
    task_type: paper_writing
    file: abstract.tex
    description: >
      (a) Lead with paradox: "formal verification + self-extraction = vacuous."
      (b) Mention the information bottleneck / d-separation briefly.
      (c) Add power caveat.
      (d) Soften cross-architecture.
      (e) Max 3-4 key numbers. Spell out SCB.
      (f) ~220 words.

  - step: 9
    task: "Consistency check + compile + page management"
    task_type: verification
    description: >
      (a) check_paper_consistency → fix cross-section issues.
      (b) Compile → verify 8-page compliance.
      (c) If over 8 pages: apply overflow_strategy.
      (d) Visual check: display item distribution on every page spread.
      (e) Abbreviation audit: confirm ≤6 in main text.
      (f) Theory coherence: §3.2 → §5 → §6 references chain.

  - step: 10
    task: "Submit to Reviewer"
    task_type: review
    description: >
      paper_agent_request_review with restructuring context.
      Focus areas: (1) theoretical depth and rigor of §3.2,
      (2) narrative clarity, (3) display item distribution,
      (4) claim strength calibration, (5) abbreviation reduction,
      (6) overall coherence of theory → empirics → escape arc.

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Setup}
\label{sec:exp-setup}

We evaluate SICA against Self-Consistency (SC) across six models, three reasoning domains, and over 3,000 condition-evaluations (${\sim}$1,250 unique instances), with diagnostic analyses of confirmation bias and process-level independence (\S\ref{sec:analysis}).

\paragraph{Models.} Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-14B (non-thinking mode)~\citep{yang2024qwen25}, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3~\citep{jiang2023mistral}, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct~\citep{dubey2024llama3}, and QwQ-32B~\citep{qwen2024qwq} (7B--32B). We additionally evaluate SCB universality via cross-model extraction on five frontier models (gpt-4o, gpt-4.1, gpt-5.5, o3, Gemini-2.5-Pro; Table~\ref{tab:frontier-scb}), where Mistral-7B extracts constraints from the target model's traces since closed-source APIs do not expose internals suitable for self-extraction.

\paragraph{Datasets.} FOLIO~\citep{han2022folio} ($n{=}204$, with gold logical annotations), ProofWriter depth-5~\citep{tafjord2021proofwriter} ($n{=}600$), LogiQA~\citep{liu2020logiqa} ($n{=}200$). StrategyQA~\citep{geva2021strategyqa} ($n{=}200$) serves as a domain-formalizability diagnostic. GSM8K~\citep{cobbe2021gsm8k} (exploratory, $n{=}30$) and AIME 2024 ($n{=}22$) probe the degenerate regime ($C_0 < 5\%$).

\paragraph{Parameters.} $K{=}12$ traces at $T{=}0.7$, extraction at $T_{\text{ext}}{=}0.3$, $\alpha{=}0.5$, Z3 timeout 10s. McNemar exact test ($\alpha{=}0.05$); 95\% bootstrap CIs ($10{,}000$ resamples) for $n \geq 200$. SICA incurs $4.5{\times}$ SC wall-clock; extraction accounts for 76\% of overhead.


\subsection{Main Results}
\label{sec:main-results}

Table~\ref{tab:main_results} reports accuracy across all conditions sorted by SC baseline, revealing three observation-driven accuracy regimes.

# V4.1 STRATEGIC RESTRUCTURE + THEORETICAL DEPTH
# Target: EMNLP 2026 ARR May cycle, DDL 2026-05-25
# Updated: 2026-05-23T17:30:00Z

meta:
  venue: EMNLP 2026
  track: main (ARR May cycle)
  template: docs/paper/acl.sty
  page_limit: 8
  deadline: 2026-05-25
  title: >
    Beyond Self-Consistency: Why Self-Extracted Constraints
    Fail to Improve LLM Logical Reasoning
  title_alternative: >
    The Symbolic Mirage: Why Formal Self-Verification
    Adds No Information Beyond Majority Voting
  title_note: >
    Alternative title is punchier and highlights the paradox.
    Director decides. Current title is safe; alternative is higher-impact.
  core_claim: >
    Provably sound Z3 verification becomes informationally vacuous
    under self-extraction: MAX-SAT agrees with majority voting on
    94.4% of problems because self-extracted constraints inherit
    the model's distributional bias (BR 1.66-4.97x across nine models).
    Three zero-cost diagnostics classify all 60 tested conditions.
    Cross-architecture NLI provides preliminary evidence of escaping
    the bottleneck.
  paper_type: >
    Diagnostic negative-result paper with constructive escape.
    Primary value: quantified diagnosis + practitioner framework.
  previous_version: "v3 (2026-05-20): G+R Dual Method (abandoned)"
  change_rationale: >
    Round 14 scored 3.5. Soundness 4/5 but Significance (2.5-3.5)
    and Presentation drag. V4.1 combines presentation restructuring
    with four theoretical depth enhancements (A/B/C/D) to upgrade
    SCB from empirical observation to theoretical result:
    (1) SCB probabilistic proof, (2) CIL information-theoretic
    framework, (3) Capability gap derivation, (4) Causal DAG.
    Quality over speed.

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# DIAGNOSIS: 7 Problems → 7 Solutions
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
restructure_rationale:

  problem_1_info_density:
    issue: "13 technical abbreviations in 8 pages"
    solution: "Reduce to 6 essential abbreviations"
    keep: [SC, SICA, BR, "K_eff", NLI, MAX-SAT]
    eliminate:
      - SCB: "spell out 'symbolic confirmation bias' (use abbreviation only in tables)"
      - CJT: "spell out 'Condorcet Jury Theorem' (only used 2-3 times)"
      - CCR: "appendix only"
      - DRC: "appendix only"
      - ICG: "spell out 'iterative constraint generation'"
      - ProcessSim: "use 'process similarity'"
      - TOST: "spell out or remove from main text"
      - FOL: "use 'logical constraints' or spell out"
    net_reduction: "13 → 6 abbreviations (-54%)"

  problem_2_depth_imbalance:
    issue: "§3.1 CJT (half page, non-original) vs §5.4 Remediation (15 lines, major finding) vs §7 Discussion (1/3 page)"
    solution: |
      - CJT: 2 sentences in intro (save 0.4 pages)
      - Remediation: expand to 25-30 lines (independence-accuracy trade-off is key)
      - Discussion: expand from 2 to 4 paragraphs (diagnostics 60/60 is strongest practical contribution)
      - Mirage Hypothesis: remove from §3, present in §5 emerging from data

  problem_3_text_wall:
    issue: "Pages 3-5 have zero display items (Related Work + Background & Setup)"
    solution: |
      - Move experimental setup into §3 Method → Table 1 appears ~page 4-5 (was page 6)
      - Move regime scatter figure into §4 Results → visual relief on page 5
      - Add diagnostic decision tree figure in §5 → another display item
      - Net: every 2-page spread gets at least one display item

  problem_4_mirage_hypothesis:
    issue: "Empirical Finding 1-2 are post-hoc observations in theorem-like boxes; only P1 is testable"
    solution: |
      - Remove Finding 1 and Finding 2 tcolorboxes from §3
      - Remove O1/O2/P1 labels (too formulaic for observations)
      - Present the Mirage Hypothesis in §5 AFTER showing SCB data
      - Frame as: "Three patterns emerge from the data → we formulate the Symbolic Mirage"
      - The hypothesis is then TESTED by §6 (cross-architecture)
      - More natural scientific narrative: data → hypothesis → test

  problem_5_cross_arch_overstatement:
    issue: "Cross-architecture results treated as established finding; only Mistral-7B is significant"
    solution: |
      - "escapes the bottleneck" → "preliminary evidence of escaping"
      - "validates" → "is consistent with"
      - Add explicit caveat: "significant only for Mistral-7B (SC below verifier)"
      - In abstract: add "on the weakest generator" qualifier
      - Section title: "Escaping the Bottleneck" → keep (describes aspiration)

  problem_6_power_caveat:
    issue: "10/16 conditions underpowered; abstract doesn't acknowledge"
    solution: |
      - Abstract: add "with equivalence established in four conditions,
        ten remaining underpowered for effects below ~2 percentage points"
      - Results: keep existing TOST discussion but condense to essentials

  problem_7_surprise:
    issue: "Core finding predictable after Huang et al.; Z3 specificity underemphasized"
    solution: |
      Reframe the hook throughout the paper:
      - OLD: "Another self-correction failure study"
      - NEW: "Even provably sound formal verification becomes vacuous under self-extraction"
      Key differentiators to emphasize:
      1. Z3 is a FORMAL solver (not another LLM trick) — provably correct
      2. 99% of constraints pass Z3 validation — no syntax issues
      3. Oracle controls prove the MECHANISM works (+30pp possible)
      4. The failure is specifically in EXTRACTION — new kind of bias
      5. MAX-SAT = majority voting on 94.4% of problems — the formal apparatus is a "mirage"
      This is distinct from Huang: they show NL self-correction fails;
      we show FORMAL self-verification fails even with a correct solver.

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# THEORETICAL DEPTH ENHANCEMENTS (A/B/C/D)
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
theoretical_enhancements:

  A_scb_proof:
    priority: highest
    placement: "§3.2 (The Information Bottleneck)"
    space_cost: "~5 lines + 1 equation = ~0.10 pages"
    core_argument: |
      Proposition (BR ≥ 1 under same-trace coupling):
      When a_M ≠ a* (model errs), n_M > n_* by definition of majority.
      Under same-trace coupling (constraint c supports its source trace's
      answer), |C_{a_M}| ∝ n_M and |C_{a*}| ∝ n_*.
      Therefore BR = n_M / n_* > 1.
      This is a mathematical necessity, not an empirical finding.
    key_equation: >
      BR = |C_{a_M}| / |C_{a*}| = n_M / n_* > 1
      (when a_M ≠ a*, by definition of majority voting)
    validation: >
      Shuffle control: BR_null ≈ BR_obs (p > 0.7) confirms the bias
      is structural — proportional to trace-count distribution, not
      extraction-specific error.
    elegance_note: >
      The proof is 3 lines. Core insight: constraints are a lossy function
      of traces that already contain the answer. BR > 1 follows from the
      definition of majority voting. No assumptions about model capability.

  B_cil:
    priority: high
    placement: "§3.2 (definition) + §5/§6 (empirical)"
    space_cost: "~4 lines + 1 equation = ~0.08 pages"
    definition: |
      CIL(V, G) = I(V_output; GT | G_answer)
      "How much does the verifier add beyond the generator's answer?"
    theoretical_predictions:
      self_extraction: >
        CIL ≈ 0. By the causal DAG (D), C ⊥ GT | A, so self-extracted
        constraints contain no information about ground truth beyond
        the generator's answer. This is the information-theoretic
        restatement of SCB.
      cross_architecture: >
        CIL > 0 when V has an independent information path to GT
        (i.e., V does not share M's distributional prior).
    operationalization: >
      CIL is the theoretical ideal. We operationalize it through the
      Conditional Correction Ratio (CCR; Appendix D):
      CCR(V,G) = log[P(V correct | G wrong) / P(V correct | G correct)]
      CCR > 0 ↔ CIL > 0 (verifier preferentially corrects errors).
      Empirical CCR correlates with combo gain: ρ = 0.84, p = 0.014.
    data_needs: >
      No new computation needed. Existing CCR data (8 conditions in
      Appendix D) serves as the empirical proxy. The d-separation
      argument gives CIL ≈ 0 for self-extraction theoretically.
      OPTIONAL: Agent could compute actual MI values from per-problem
      (G_answer, V_output, GT) tuples in combo data for a cleaner
      presentation. Flag as nice-to-have, not blocking.

  C_capability_gap:
    priority: medium
    placement: "§6.1 (before empirical results)"
    space_cost: "~5 lines + 1 equation = ~0.10 pages"
    derivation: |
      Under conditional independence between G (accuracy SC_G) and V
      (accuracy V_acc):
      ΔCombo ≈ (1 - SC_G) · V_acc - SC_G · (1 - V_acc)
             = V_acc - SC_G
      Properties:
      - Monotonically decreasing in SC_G ✓
      - ΔCombo = 0 when SC_G = V_acc (breakeven at capability parity) ✓
      - ΔCombo > 0 when SC_G < V_acc (verifier stronger) ✓
      - As SC_G → 1, gain → 0 (ceiling: few errors to correct) ✓
    empirical_validation: >
      DeBERTa standalone V_acc = 55%. Model predicts breakeven at
      SC_G ≈ 55%. Empirically: Mistral (SC 39%) gains (+7pp),
      all generators above 72% show no significant gain.
      Spearman ρ = 1.0, p = 0.003, n=6 matches the monotonic prediction.
      Magnitude attenuated vs linear model due to imperfect independence
      and vote-weighting mechanics — state this as expected.
    note: >
      This is a first-order approximation. State it as such:
      "Under a simplified independence model..." with the caveat that
      real combo voting involves weighted margins.

  D_causal_dag:
    priority: highest
    placement: "§3.2 (The Information Bottleneck) — as Figure"
    space_cost: "~0.20 pages (TikZ figure, single-column)"
    dag_structure: |
      Self-extraction DAG:
        Q → GT (ground truth)
        Q, M → T (trace)
        T → A (answer, contained in trace)
        T, M → C (constraint, extracted by same model)
        {A, C} → S (MAX-SAT score)

      d-separation: C ⊥ GT | A
      All paths from C to GT: C ← (T,M) ← Q → GT
      Conditioning on A (which is T → A) blocks the chain.
      Interpretation: constraints carry no information about GT
      beyond what's already in the answer.
    cross_arch_contrast: |
      Cross-architecture DAG:
        Q → GT
        Q, M_G → T → A → S
        Q, M_V → V_out → S (independent path)

      V_out ⊥̸ GT | A because V has an independent path Q → M_V → V_out
      that doesn't pass through A. Hence CIL > 0.
    figure_design: >
      Two-panel TikZ figure (a) Self-extraction (b) Cross-architecture.
      Panel (a): show A as an information bottleneck node (highlighted).
      Panel (b): show V_out with independent path to GT (highlighted).
      Compact, ~0.5 column width per panel. Breaks pages 3-4 text wall.
      Gray/blue color scheme matching Figure 1.
